evidence.quote: The Håga Mound is a Bronze Age burial mound (tumulus) in Sweden, at Uppsala [SUPPORTED: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H%C3%A5ga_mound]; The mound is built of turf laid on top of a cairn [SUPPORTED: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H%C3%A5ga_mound]; Under the cairn lay a wooden chamber [SUPPORTED: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H%C3%A5ga_mound]; The wooden chamber held a hollow oak coffin [SUPPORTED: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H%C3%A5ga_mound]; The coffin held cremated remains [SUPPORTED: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H%C3%A5ga_mound]; The cremated remains were those of a short man [SUPPORTED: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H%C3%A5ga_mound]; It is Scandinavia's most gold-rich Bronze Age grave ever found [SUPPORTED: https://historiska.se/en/explore-history/history-hub/the-haga-mound/]
